source.title: Representation learnt by SGD and Adaptive learning rules - Conditions that Vary Sparsity and Selectivity in Neural Network

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full dissertation, though its title wording differs slightly from the catalog title.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies optimizer, batch size, hidden-layer width, and convolutional architecture and reports test accuracy on MNIST; these are conceptual tests of some mapped conditions, with different models and measurements from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy alongside sparsity and selectivity. Sparsity and selectivity results alone do not measure the claim versions. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Own MNIST test-accuracy comparisons test convolutional versus fully connected architectures (V3), adaptive optimizers versus SGD (V4), and batch size under a fixed 30-epoch budget (V5). Width experiments do not establish training interpolation or convergence, so they do not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but incomplete. The author concludes that sparsity, selectivity, and test accuracy often vary together but cannot reliably predict one another. Smaller batches improve the reported momentum-free SGD accuracy, whereas very small Adam batches and SGD combined with high momentum provide exceptions. Adding the tested convolutional component improves accuracy except with Adagrad.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a sigmoid feed-forward MNIST classifier and reports test accuracy, rather than random-label memorization or the specified benchmark and architecture setups. The convolutional comparison adds a convolutional layer to the feed-forward baseline.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by optimizer: adding a convolutional layer does not improve the reported Adagrad result, and the batch-size result depends on optimizer. The author also reports that combining batch size 1 with momentum 0.9 does not always improve SGD test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation sparsity and class selectivity can change independently of one another and of test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hoyer activation sparsity and CCMAS class selectivity do not reliably predict MNIST test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing sigmoid hidden-layer width usually improves test accuracy, except for SGD at batch size 50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width affects held-out accuracy in these finite-budget sigmoid networks, with optimizer and batch-size dependence; improvement beyond interpolation is not established.

record.problems: MNIST only; the study measures generalization ability by test accuracy and notes that train and test loss would provide a more robust measure. Most condition-sweep values are presented in figures, and the author reports three runs with mean and standard error. The author also notes limitations in the multi-layer sparsity/selectivity calculation.
record.rows_left_out: The study contains many additional optimizer-by-batch-size and neuron-count conditions, mostly reported only in figures. They were not extracted because the prose does not assign exact test-accuracy values to each condition; included the stated aggregate trends and explicit exceptions instead.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
The sigmoid width sweep reports test accuracy but establishes neither zero training error nor convergence or widths beyond interpolation.
MNIST is tested. Other datasets, isolation of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, and initialization from a trained convolutional network are untested.
Language benchmarks, matched training performance, decay-schedule tuning, systematic broader tuning comparisons, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD are untested.
Language models, recovery through longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and normalization or regularization adaptations are untested.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, sharpness ranking, or measured training-test error gaps.
No identification or removal of memorized training examples and no random-removal control.

missing.what: Matched optimizer comparisons across hidden-layer depths, including adaptive-method advantages at batch 50 and Adagrad's failure at four layers. These numerical results are not covered by the declared omitted batch-size and neuron-count sweeps.

Adam's test accuracy slightly decreases at batch sizes 1 and 5, and batch 1 performs worse than baseline Adam at batch 50. This explicit prose result materially qualifies the extracted SGD-only batch trend.

Combining SGD batch size 1 with momentum 0.9 reduces test accuracy relative to both component configurations. Record the matched conditions and verify the training budget, which is not explicitly specified in this section.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Results are reported as means and standard errors over three runs. Supplied figure captions contain no readable plotted values, so qualitative prose supports those comparisons without establishing effect sizes or significance. Learning rates were searched separately for each optimizer; most other settings remained at defaults. Test accuracy was also used to select learning rates, with no separate validation split described.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or report random-label fit or held-out accuracy.
Width is varied, but the study does not report zero training error or establish widths beyond the interpolation threshold; it uses sigmoid rather than ReLU networks.
Tests adding a convolutional layer to a feed-forward MNIST model, not the stated image datasets, local-connectivity mechanism, sparse learned connections, or convolutional initialization.
Compares SGD and adaptive optimizers on MNIST, not the listed image and language benchmarks or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching recipes.
Varies batch size on MNIST with a fixed 30-epoch budget in the main sweep; does not test language models or the cited recipe adaptations.
Measures activation sparsity and selectivity, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the training-test error gap.
Does not identify memorized examples, remove examples, or compare retraining with random-example removal.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated October 2024, although the record lists 2022. Exact convolution and batch-sweep accuracies are unavailable in the extracted figures; R7 duplicates R5's optimizer finding.

statements.correction: Table 5.3: batch 50, Adam and Adadelta exceed SGD accuracy at each matched depth from one through four hidden layers. Sections 5.6.2 and 5.7.3: the single-hidden-layer SGD model outperforms the other optimizers at batch 1. These comparisons do not establish a batch-dependent reversal at every depth.
statements.problem: The wording implies a batch-1 hidden-layer sweep. The depth sweep uses batch 50; the batch-1 SGD advantage comes from separate single-hidden-layer experiments.
